title: Build the AI GTM Agent That Knows the Buyer - Dr. Sajjan Kanukolanu, Position2 (Position Squared)
talk_summary: A GTM (go-to-market) talk about building a three-layer architecture (signals, buyer intelligence, action) with connected agents to identify anonymous website visitors and personalize outreach.

takeaways.technique: Staged agent pipeline with filter gates between stages
takeaways.what_they_do: A chain of single-purpose agents (identify → enrich → ICP filter → match → action) where each stage filters/dedupes before passing a clean set to the next, and tools can be swapped without changing the architecture.
takeaways.evidence_quote: no single tool catches every visitor... consolidate them, and dedupe them, and send it over to the next layer

takeaways.technique: Quarterly retraining of knowledge base from closed outcomes
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat the knowledge base as the source of truth for agent decisions and refresh it every quarter with closed-won/closed-lost data to prevent 'ICP drift' where agents act on stale criteria.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You retrain your agents every quarter with your closed one or closed lost opportunities

takeaways.technique: Separate fit score from intent score
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly avoid conflating two different scoring dimensions, arguing that combining them sends the wrong signal to the wrong recipient.
takeaways.evidence_quote: score fit and intent needs to be looked at separately. Conflating them is going to send the wrong message to the wrong person

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately suppress low-value alerts so humans keep trusting the system, using the knowledge base/context to cut noise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If everything is flagged as hot to a sales rep, they would stop acting... they stop trusting the system and the system's dead

takeaways.technique: One-click approval to avoid human bottleneck
takeaways.what_they_do: They measure the friction of human approval and set a hard threshold: if editing an AI draft takes longer than ~30 seconds, the initiative dies because humans revert to doing it themselves.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the time taken to edit an email that the AI writes is... longer than 30 seconds, then this is a dead initiative

takeaways.what_they_do: They build a policy layer so non-developers can audit which agent/stage broke and fix it themselves, rather than filing a dev ticket.
